scenarioStory.history: Coworker noticed the patient did not respond to a page for a 2:00 PM meeting. When she checked on him roughly ten minutes later, she found him slumped forward in his desk chair, not responding to her voice, but breathing on his own with loud snoring respirations. No known witnessed collapse, no reported seizure activity, no vomiting noted by the coworker.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 47-year-old male slumped forward in his desk chair. He does not respond to his name or verbal commands but is breathing with loud, snoring respirations. A coworker is present with limited history. → Primary survey completed: The crew has completed a rapid primary survey and confirmed a blood glucose of 38 mg/dL. The patient remains unresponsive to voice, breathing but unable to protect his own airway, so oral glucose cannot be safely given. → Rapid transport initiated: The patient is packaged, positioned laterally, receiving supplemental oxygen, and en route to the closest appropriate receiving facility with an ALS intercept requested for dextrose administration. Vital signs and mental status are reassessed en route.

relatedChecklist: Assess airway patency; reposition patient to open airway

scenarioEvents.name: Primary survey completed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew has completed a rapid primary survey and confirmed a blood glucose of 38 mg/dL. The patient remains unresponsive to voice, breathing but unable to protect his own airway, so oral glucose cannot be safely given.
relatedChecklist: Recognize oral glucose contraindicated; patient cannot protect his airway
Position patient laterally to protect airway and limit aspiration risk

scenarioEvents.name: Rapid transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: The patient is packaged, positioned laterally, receiving supplemental oxygen, and en route to the closest appropriate receiving facility with an ALS intercept requested for dextrose administration. Vital signs and mental status are reassessed en route.
relatedChecklist: Transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
Reassess vital signs and mental status en route

scenarioEvents.name: Primary survey delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Assessment and airway repositioning were delayed. The patient's positional airway obstruction has progressed: breathing is now irregular with audible gurgling, and oxygenation is dropping.
relatedChecklist: Suction airway immediately to clear pooled secretions
Open airway with head tilt/chin lift and reposition immediately
